old_caption: The video captures a dance class taking place in a spacious studio with mirrored walls and a light-colored floor. The instructor, positioned on the left side of the frame, leads a group of dancers through a choreographed routine. She is dressed in a light blue top and beige pants, her movements fluid and precise. The dancers, wearing a mix of casual and dance attire, follow her lead, mirroring her gestures and steps. The studio is well-lit by overhead fluorescent lights, creating a bright and focused environment for the practice session. In the background, a television screen is mounted on the wall, though it appears to be turned off during the video. Various pieces of equipment, such as a barre and a music stand, are visible along the edges of the room, indicating a well-equipped space for dance rehearsals. The dancers' synchronized movements and the instructor's guidance suggest a structured and dedicated practice session.

caption: The video captures a dance rehearsal room with a wall-to-wall mirror, overhead fluorescent panels, and a ballet barre along the left wall. In the foreground a woman in a blue-grey sheer top and beige wide-leg trousers performs a slow arm-and-hand sequence, seen from the side, the figure facing the camera being her mirror reflection. Her hands start drawn near her face, one cupped by the mouth, then gather at the chest. One hand opens palm-up forward while the other rises, and her right arm lifts to a high overhead position. That arm then sweeps outward and across as her torso rotates so her back turns more toward the camera. Her legs shift from a closed stance into a wide lunged stance, and one foot lifts near the final frame. The mirror reflection tracks these changes, while reflected participants in white tops and grey trousers and one in black move their arms from bent positions near the head toward overhead reaches. Ceiling lights, mirror seams and the barre keep constant positions, indicating a stationary camera.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
